correctness.rationale: The derivative identity is an algebraic identity for every n>=2,beta>1; the value/derivative Gram determinant is positive. The derivative factors have precisely three ordered roots, with sign pattern +,-,+,-; endpoint limits 0 imply complete sharp classification. Exact integer-weight Gram/derivative assertions passed 1010 tests; real-weight continuum rests on analytic proof. Stirling and strict artanh inequality prove the eventual smaller-radius winner and Gamma law. Does not prove finite-degree smaller-radius superiority or general multi-node optimality.

value.rationale: The geometry of a repeated sampling site provides exactly two independent measurements, value and first derivative. Sharp capture of a prescribed Fourier/Bergman monomial is an intrinsic measure of detectability by a minimal jet. This result gives an exact two-candidate optimizer for every degree and admissible standard weight, locates a nontrivial intervening valley, and proves a one-sided Gamma-boundary selection and sharp constant. It is not merely normalizing a known Gram matrix: the factorization and strict global asymptotic comparison resolve the finite search and the high-degree sampling loss; the Fock model has a qualitatively different two-shell asymptotic.
